norms.what: The orchestrator is `user-invocable: false` so the entry commands and the stages can invoke it through the Skill tool, which Claude Code blocks for a `disable-model-invocation` skill; the price is that Claude can also invoke it on its own, and no frontmatter keeps it out of unrelated tasks. The guard makes a mistaken invocation cost one skill load and change nothing. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #38).

The arguments answer the plan gate and stop the run at the report, so the audit can run headless and in a plugin eval suite; no argument approves applying changes. The grammar is unchanged from the per-transition audits; the transition itself now comes first, passed by the entry point. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N63` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N63` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #38).

A new transition is a new knowledge file, not a new skill. Resolving it beside the orchestrator with `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` works both from the plugin and in a copied install, where `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is not substituted. With no file, the audit still runs on the docs alone, so it is useful before the knowledge exists. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #38).

Each stage is its own skill, so the run's state must live on disk: the stages read the run file to know they may run, and a resume after an interruption or a compaction reads it to know where to continue. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #38). In 0.6.0 the run's files moved from `.claude/audits/` to their own folder under `.model-audits/`: Claude Code protects all of `.claude/` from writes in every permission mode but bypass, and allow rules do not pre-approve them, so a headless smoke run in `acceptEdits` stopped before the plan and every user outside auto mode got a prompt per write (#57).

The flow is split into stage skills so each stays within the size a skill keeps after compaction and loads only when reached: a run cancelled at the plan loads only the entry, this skill and the plan. The name the Skill tool lists differs between the plugin and a copied install. Written for the transition-agnostic audit (#34, #38).

A long audit can be interrupted by an API error or compacted; after compaction only the first 5,000 tokens of each re-attached skill survive, in a shared 25,000, oldest dropped first, and the orchestrator is the oldest skill of the run. Continuing from the files on disk avoids redoing finished batches or edits. Derived from `audit-sonnet-5-5` `N47` and `audit-opus-5-5` `N47` at inbrace-config@0.5.0; history in git. Every file the run writes goes by its absolute path under the run's folder, so nothing lands in the user's tree (#34, #61).
